## Original problem (task)
[01274f41553299e7] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

BODY
The conflict stems from a combination of linguistic ambiguity in agreements and a breakdown in communication channels. The disagreement over 'what the agreement meant' suggests that the household is relying on implicit expectations rather than explicit definitions. This is exacerbated by fluctuating schedules, which introduce instability into routine, and one roommate's withdrawal from dialogue, which creates a power imbalance and prevents resolution.

To address this, the focus should shift from verbal agreements to a shared, visible record. A written chore chart or a digital shared list removes the ambiguity of interpretation. However, the primary obstacle is the friend avoiding conversations. Forcing a confrontation may increase tension; instead, introducing a low-friction, asynchronous system for coordination (like a messaging group or a physical whiteboard) allows the avoiding party to participate without the pressure of a face-to-face meeting. The goal is to decouple the administration of the flat from the emotional tension of the arguments.
COMMITMENTS
I propose the implementation of a written or digital tracking system to eliminate semantic disputes over agreements. This involves a commitment to define chores explicitly rather than generally. I suggest a transition to asynchronous communication to re-engage the avoiding roommate, though this remains an unresolved problem if the individual refuses all forms of coordination. The success of this approach depends on the willingness of the other two roommates to maintain the record consistently.

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
